hook.text: Einstein's most famous equation says mass and energy are the same thing—interchangeable at a stunning exchange rate.

buildup.text: c² is the speed of light squared—about 9 × 10¹⁶ m²/s². A tiny amount of mass contains enormous energy.

discovery.text: One kilogram of matter fully converted to energy would yield 90 quadrillion joules—equal to a 21-megaton bomb.

twist.text: Nuclear reactors convert less than 1% of fuel mass to energy—yet that's still millions of times more than burning coal.

climax.text: The Sun converts 4 million tons of mass into energy every second—and has enough fuel for another 5 billion years.

punchline.text: Mass is frozen energy—and the exchange rate is astronomical.

quiz.question: How much mass does the Sun convert to energy per second?
